name.sw: Afya Shule

delivery_rule.en: One box every two months, packed with two months of goods. Delivered on its own it pays its way on every plan except: Holiday box (May and November) on the 12-month plan. Those boxes ride inside another Afya box delivered to the same household (one delivery, no extra delivery cost) or are collected in store. Monthly delivery is not offered: a one-month basket cannot carry packing and delivery.
delivery_rule.sw: Sanduku moja kila baada ya miezi miwili, lenye bidhaa za miezi miwili. Likiletwa peke yake linalipa gharama zake kwenye kila mpango isipokuwa: Sanduku la likizo (Mei na Novemba) kwenye mpango wa miezi 12. Masanduku hayo husafirishwa ndani ya sanduku lingine la Afya linaloletwa kwa kaya hiyohiyo (usafirishaji mmoja, bila gharama ya ziada ya usafirishaji) au huchukuliwa dukani. Kuleta kila mwezi hakutolewi: kikapu cha mwezi mmoja hakiwezi kubeba gharama za kufunga na kusafirisha.

who.en:
Afya Shule is the school-year box for a child aged 4 to 12 in Dar es Salaam, from the first year of pre-primary school to the end of primary school. It arrives every two months, timed to the school calendar: a big box in January for the start of the year, term boxes in March, July and September, and holiday boxes in May and November that carry play and travel items for the June and December holidays.

Why these items. The common illnesses of school-age children in Tanzania are the ones that clean hands, clean teeth, a net and periodic deworming prevent. WHO recommends periodic deworming of all school-age children where soil-transmitted worms are common, and Tanzania gives it free in school campaigns; the box reminds parents before each holiday and the partner pharmacy covers a missed round. WHO advises twice-daily brushing with a 1,000–1,500 ppm fluoride toothpaste, which matters most once the first permanent molars come through at about six. Insecticide-treated nets are one of WHO’s two core malaria protections, and many nets sold in shops are untreated. Safe water, sanitation and handwashing with soap prevent diarrhoea (WHO). Tanzania’s school health and school WASH guidelines set the hygiene the morning inspection checks: clean body, short hair, short nails.

Learning and play. Exercise books and pencils run out every few weeks, so the term boxes bring them. WHO asks for about an hour of activity a day for children; in the holidays a ball replaces the school timetable.

What it does not do. Medicines in the box list (deworming tablet, paracetamol syrup, ORS) are supplied only by the licensed partner pharmacy, on its advice, and are not priced in the box. Food is not assigned: porridge flour and snacks are chosen by the parent from the nutrition shelf.
who.sw:
Afya Shule ni sanduku la mwaka wa shule kwa mtoto wa miaka 4 hadi 12 jijini Dar es Salaam, kuanzia mwaka wa kwanza wa elimu ya awali hadi mwisho wa shule ya msingi. Linakuja kila baada ya miezi miwili, likifuata kalenda ya shule: sanduku kubwa Januari kwa mwanzo wa mwaka, masanduku ya muhula Machi, Julai na Septemba, na masanduku ya likizo Mei na Novemba yenye vitu vya kuchezea na vya safari kwa likizo za Juni na Desemba.

Kwa nini vitu hivi. Magonjwa ya kawaida ya watoto wa umri wa shule Tanzania ni yale yanayozuiwa na mikono safi, meno safi, chandarua na dawa za minyoo kwa vipindi. WHO inapendekeza dawa za minyoo kwa vipindi kwa watoto wote wa umri wa shule pale minyoo ya udongoni ilipo kwa wingi, na Tanzania huzitoa bure katika kampeni za shule; sanduku huwakumbusha wazazi kabla ya kila likizo na famasia mshirika hushughulikia awamu iliyokosekana. WHO inashauri kupiga mswaki mara mbili kwa siku kwa dawa ya meno yenye floraidi ya ppm 1,000–1,500, jambo muhimu zaidi magego ya kwanza ya kudumu yanapoota karibu na miaka sita. Vyandarua vyenye dawa ni mojawapo ya kinga kuu mbili za malaria za WHO, na vyandarua vingi vinavyouzwa madukani havina dawa. Maji salama, vyoo na kunawa mikono kwa sabuni huzuia kuhara (WHO). Miongozo ya Tanzania ya huduma za afya shuleni na ya maji, usafi wa mazingira na usafi shuleni inaweka usafi unaokaguliwa asubuhi: mwili safi, nywele fupi, kucha fupi.

Kujifunza na kucheza. Madaftari na penseli huisha kila baada ya wiki chache, hivyo masanduku ya muhula huyaleta. WHO inataka watoto wafanye shughuli za mwili takriban saa moja kwa siku; likizoni mpira huchukua nafasi ya ratiba ya shule.

Lisichofanya. Dawa zilizo kwenye orodha ya sanduku (kidonge cha minyoo, sharubati ya paracetamol, ORS) hutolewa na famasia mshirika yenye leseni tu, kwa ushauri wake, na hazina bei ndani ya sanduku. Chakula hakipangwi: unga wa uji na vitafunio huchaguliwa na mzazi kutoka rafu ya lishe.

clinic_line.en: Any medicine for your child, its dose for the child’s weight, and whether a deworming dose is needed outside the school campaign are decided by your clinic or the partner pharmacist. A fever in Tanzania needs a malaria test the same day; a child who cannot drink, is very drowsy or has blood in the stool goes to a clinic at once.
clinic_line.sw: Dawa yoyote kwa mtoto wako, dozi yake kulingana na uzito wa mtoto, na kama dozi ya minyoo inahitajika nje ya kampeni ya shule huamuliwa na kliniki yako au mfamasia mshirika. Homa Tanzania inahitaji kipimo cha malaria siku hiyohiyo; mtoto asiyeweza kunywa, anayesinzia sana au mwenye damu kwenye kinyesi apelekwe kliniki mara moja.

name.sw: Sabuni laini ya kuogea

why.en: A school child in Dar es Salaam heat usually bathes twice a day, after school and after play especially. Plain washing with soap and water is enough for daily hygiene; antibacterial soaps are not needed and can dry young skin. A mild, low-fragrance bar is the default.
why.sw: Mtoto wa shule katika joto la Dar es Salaam kwa kawaida huoga mara mbili kwa siku, hasa baada ya shule na baada ya kucheza. Kuoga kwa sabuni na maji kunatosha kwa usafi wa kila siku; sabuni za kuua vijidudu hazihitajiki na zinaweza kukausha ngozi changa. Kipande laini chenye manukato kidogo ndicho chaguo la msingi.

items.qty_formula: 2 baths a day × 60 days × about 3 g a bath ≈ 360 g → two 175 g bars = 350 g (planning assumption)

name.en: Mild hair wash, tear-free for younger children
name.sw: Shampuu laini ya nywele, isiyowasha macho kwa watoto wadogo

why.en: Most Tanzanian primary schools ask for short, clean hair. A dusty playground and daily sweat mean the hair needs washing about twice a week. Regular washing and a clean comb help against scalp ringworm and lice, which spread in classrooms; a medicated shampoo is only for a diagnosis made by a clinician.
why.sw: Shule nyingi za msingi Tanzania zinataka nywele fupi na safi. Uwanja wenye vumbi na jasho la kila siku humaanisha nywele zioshwe takriban mara mbili kwa wiki. Kuosha mara kwa mara na kitana safi husaidia dhidi ya mba wa fangasi na chawa, wanaosambaa darasani; shampuu ya dawa ni kwa ugonjwa uliothibitishwa na mtaalamu wa afya tu.

items.qty_formula: 2 washes a week × 8.7 weeks × about 8 ml a wash ≈ 140 ml (planning assumption)

why.sw: Baada ya kuoga, safu nyembamba huzuia ngozi changa kukauka na kupasuka, hasa viwiko, magoti na miguu wakati wa kiangazi chenye vumbi. Mafuta ya mgando ya kawaida ni nafuu, hayana manukato na yanatosha kwa watoto wengi.

name.sw: Kitakasa mikono cha mfukoni kwa shule

why.en: Clean hands before eating and after the toilet cut diarrhoea and respiratory infections, and many schools have water but no soap at the taps. Soap and water come first; a pocket gel covers the times there is none. Adults should keep it out of reach of children under six, who must use it only under supervision.
why.sw: Mikono safi kabla ya kula na baada ya kutoka chooni hupunguza kuhara na maambukizi ya njia ya hewa, na shule nyingi zina maji lakini hazina sabuni kwenye mabomba. Sabuni na maji ni ya kwanza; jeli ya mfukoni ni kwa nyakati ambazo hazipo. Watoto chini ya miaka sita waitumie chini ya uangalizi wa mtu mzima tu.

items.qty_formula: about 2 uses × 1 ml × 20 school days = 40 ml a school month × 2

name.sw: Dawa ya kufukuza mbu kwa jioni

why.en: Malaria is still a leading cause of child illness in Tanzania. The core protection is sleeping under an insecticide-treated net (WHO); a repellent covers the evening hours outdoors before bed. Use only a product whose label states the active ingredient and the youngest age it may be used on.
why.sw: Malaria bado ni chanzo kikuu cha ugonjwa kwa watoto Tanzania. Kinga ya msingi ni kulala ndani ya chandarua chenye dawa (WHO); dawa ya kufukuza mbu hulinda saa za jioni nje kabla ya kulala. Tumia bidhaa ambayo lebo yake inaonyesha kiambato hai na umri wa chini kabisa unaoruhusiwa tu.

why.en: Exercise books run out every few weeks and a child without one loses the lesson. Two a school month is a planning figure for a primary pupil; the parent can change the number in the app.

why.en: Grazes from the playground are the commonest school injury. Rinsing with clean water and covering the wound keeps dirt out until it heals. Twenty plasters a year in a small pouch.
why.sw: Michubuko ya uwanjani ndiyo majeraha yanayotokea zaidi shuleni. Kusuuza kwa maji safi na kufunika jeraha huzuia uchafu hadi lipone. Plasta ishirini kwa mwaka kwenye mfuko mdogo.

name.en: Insecticide-treated mosquito net for the child’s bed
name.sw: Chandarua chenye dawa kwa kitanda cha mtoto

why.en: WHO names insecticide-treated nets as one of the two core ways to prevent malaria. Many nets sold in shops are untreated, so the first box of the first year brings one long-lasting treated net for the child’s own bed; it is replaced about every three years.
why.sw: WHO inataja vyandarua vyenye dawa kuwa mojawapo ya njia mbili kuu za kuzuia malaria. Vyandarua vingi vinavyouzwa madukani havina dawa, hivyo sanduku la kwanza la mwaka wa kwanza linaleta chandarua kimoja chenye dawa ya muda mrefu kwa kitanda cha mtoto; hubadilishwa takriban kila miaka mitatu.

items.qty_formula: 1 net per child; lasts about 3 years

brands.note: Estimate: no Tanzanian online listing of a treated net was found on 10 Nov 2026; planning figure from a 2024 Tanzanian retail net price survey (median TSh 9,000–10,000 for an untreated net), as cited in the code; to be replaced by a distributor quote.

name.en: Paracetamol syrup for fever or pain (partner pharmacy)
name.sw: Sharubati ya paracetamol kwa homa au maumivu (famasia mshirika)

why.en: A bottle at home means a feverish child can be made comfortable at night. A fever in Tanzania still needs a malaria test the same day, at a clinic; paracetamol does not replace that. The dose depends on the child’s weight and is set by the pharmacist. Not priced in the box.
why.sw: Chupa nyumbani humwezesha mtoto mwenye homa kupata nafuu usiku. Homa Tanzania bado inahitaji kipimo cha malaria siku hiyohiyo, kliniki; paracetamol haichukui nafasi hiyo. Dozi hutegemea uzito wa mtoto na huwekwa na mfamasia. Haina bei ndani ya sanduku.

name.sw: Sabuni laini ya kuogea

why.en: A school child in Dar es Salaam heat usually bathes twice a day, after school and after play especially. Plain washing with soap and water is enough for daily hygiene; antibacterial soaps are not needed and can dry young skin. A mild, low-fragrance bar is the default.
why.sw: Mtoto wa shule katika joto la Dar es Salaam kwa kawaida huoga mara mbili kwa siku, hasa baada ya shule na baada ya kucheza. Kuoga kwa sabuni na maji kunatosha kwa usafi wa kila siku; sabuni za kuua vijidudu hazihitajiki na zinaweza kukausha ngozi changa. Kipande laini chenye manukato kidogo ndicho chaguo la msingi.

why.en: Most Tanzanian primary schools ask for short, clean hair. A dusty playground and daily sweat mean the hair needs washing about twice a week. Regular washing and a clean comb help against scalp ringworm and lice, which spread in classrooms; a medicated shampoo is only for a diagnosis made by a clinician.
why.sw: Shule nyingi za msingi Tanzania zinataka nywele fupi na safi. Uwanja wenye vumbi na jasho la kila siku humaanisha nywele zioshwe takriban mara mbili kwa wiki. Kuosha mara kwa mara na kitana safi husaidia dhidi ya mba wa fangasi na chawa, wanaosambaa darasani; shampuu ya dawa ni kwa ugonjwa uliothibitishwa na mtaalamu wa afya tu.

name.sw: Dawa ya meno yenye floraidi

why.en: Tooth decay is the most common disease of childhood, and the first permanent molars come through at about age six. WHO recommends brushing twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste of 1,000–1,500 ppm. A pea-sized amount is enough, spat out and not rinsed away; a parent brushes or supervises until about age seven.
why.sw: Kuoza kwa meno ndio ugonjwa unaowapata watoto zaidi, na magego ya kwanza ya kudumu huota karibu na umri wa miaka sita. WHO inapendekeza kupiga mswaki mara mbili kwa siku kwa dawa ya meno yenye floraidi ya ppm 1,000–1,500. Kiasi cha punje ya njegere kinatosha; mtoto ateme bila kusukutua. Mzazi ampigie mswaki au amsimamie hadi karibu miaka saba.

why.en: Clean hands before eating and after the toilet cut diarrhoea and respiratory infections, and many schools have water but no soap at the taps. name.en: Deworming tablet (partner pharmacy, if not given at school)
name.sw: Kidonge cha minyoo (famasia mshirika, kama hakikutolewa shuleni)

why.en: Worms caught from soil cause anaemia and poor growth. WHO recommends periodic deworming of all school-age children where worms are common, with a single albendazole 400 mg or mebendazole 500 mg dose, and Tanzania gives it free in school campaigns. The box reminds the parent before each holiday; the partner pharmacy supplies a tablet only if the child missed the school round and the pharmacist or clinic agrees. Not priced in the box.
why.sw: Minyoo inayotoka udongoni husababisha upungufu wa damu na ukuaji duni. WHO inapendekeza dawa za minyoo kwa vipindi kwa watoto wote wa umri wa shule pale minyoo ilipo kwa wingi, kwa dozi moja ya albendazole mg 400 au mebendazole mg 500, na Tanzania huitoa bure katika kampeni za shule. Sanduku humkumbusha mzazi kabla ya kila likizo; famasia mshirika hutoa kidonge tu kama mtoto alikosa awamu ya shule na mfamasia au kliniki imekubali. Haina bei ndani ya sanduku.

why.en: Holiday travel upcountry brings new water and food, and diarrhoea dehydrates a child fast. WHO names oral rehydration solution as the first treatment. A child who cannot drink, has blood in the stool or is drowsy goes to a clinic at once.
why.sw: Safari za likizo mikoani huleta maji na vyakula vipya, na kuhara humpunguzia mtoto maji mwilini haraka. WHO inataja ORS kuwa tiba ya kwanza. Mtoto asiyeweza kunywa, mwenye damu kwenye kinyesi au anayesinzia apelekwe kliniki mara moja.

tiers.en: Regular = the core box with the default brands. Premium = core + Staedtler Tradition write & draw pencil set (TSh 23,379). Luxury = core + Contigo Cortland Autoseal bottle (TSh 44,624). The premium or luxury item is its own line at shelf price, outside the saving (D4), in each box.
tiers.sw: Kawaida = sanduku la msingi lenye chapa za msingi. Premium = sanduku la msingi + Staedtler Tradition write & draw pencil set (TSh 23,379). Anasa = sanduku la msingi + Contigo Cortland Autoseal bottle (TSh 44,624). Bidhaa ya premium au ya anasa ina bei yake peke yake kwa bei ya rafu, nje ya punguzo (D4), katika kila sanduku.

services_note.en: growth-check: height, weight and BMI at the Afya Check in store when a box is collected or at any visit, free; the reading goes on a growth chart in the app, and BMI-for-age needs the WHO growth reference (to be set in R2). deworming-reminder: a reminder before the June and December holidays to check the school deworming round, free. hpv-reminder: for girls at 9, the free single-dose HPV vaccine given by the public programme, free. dental-check: a check-up every six months with a partner dentist, offered as an add-on; no partner quote yet (R7).
services_note.sw: growth-check: urefu, uzito na BMI kwenye Afya Check dukani sanduku linapochukuliwa au wakati wowote wa kutembelea, bure; kipimo huwekwa kwenye chati ya ukuaji kwenye programu, na BMI kwa umri inahitaji kipimo rejea cha ukuaji cha WHO (kitapangwa kwenye R2). deworming-reminder: kikumbusho kabla ya likizo za Juni na Desemba kukagua awamu ya dawa za minyoo shuleni, bure. hpv-reminder: kwa wasichana wa miaka 9, chanjo ya HPV ya dozi moja inayotolewa bure na mpango wa serikali, bure. dental-check: uchunguzi wa meno kila miezi sita kwa daktari wa meno mshirika, kama nyongeza; bado hakuna bei ya mshirika (R7).

pricing_rule.formula: D4 (10 Nov 2026): core price = shelf value of the box goods × (1 − 3% / 6% / 9% for the 1 / 6 / 12-month plans), nearest 500, never above shelf; packing (S 3,500 · M 5,000) and one delivery (3,500) included. Check: price − goods at landed cost (R3 shares: brand 78%, pharm 72%, own 50%) − packing − delivery − 1% points ≥ 0.
pricing_rule.note: Medicines are listed but sold by the licensed partner pharmacy and not priced in the box (B4). The premium and luxury items are their own line at shelf price, outside the saving.

open.en: The treated net is an estimate (TSh 10,000): no Tanzanian online listing of a long-lasting treated net was found. Get a distributor quote for a WHO-prequalified net.

open.en: Whitedent toothpastes are the cheapest in the range, but their listings do not state fluoride. Confirm on the pack before offering them; Colgate Maximum Protection is the default until then.

open.en: Box months follow the usual Tanzanian school year (January to December, with June and December holidays); confirm against the Ministry of Education calendar each year. Stationery is a convenience line; the founder may drop it.
open.sw: Miezi ya masanduku inafuata mwaka wa kawaida wa shule Tanzania (Januari hadi Desemba, na likizo za Juni na Desemba); ilinganishwe na kalenda ya Wizara ya Elimu kila mwaka. Vifaa vya shule ni bidhaa ya urahisi; mwanzilishi anaweza kuviondoa.
